transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-06-24
Start: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 57 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE); Priya Shah (Redwood SE); Michael Chen (Asterion, Head of ML); Sofia Ramirez (Asterion, Eng Manager); Dr. Anita Patel (Asterion, Clinical Data)

Summary (auto-generated): POC scoping for open-model shortlist for clinical QA and triage. Key success metrics are accuracy/F1 on clinical prompts, latency <300ms for short responses, throughput target ~10 req/s with burst to 25, and strict data residency/KMS requirements. Redwood to run benchmarks on provided sample set and share security docs + pricing.

--- Transcript ---
[00:00] Jordan (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining - we have about an hour. Quick intros, I'm Jordan, AE focusing on healthcare accounts. Priya's our SE, she'll own the benchmark and the technical setup.
[00:12] Michael: Hi, Michael Chen, head of ML at Asterion. We own the clinical QA pipeline and this is to scope a POC for triage+QA automation.
[00:18] Sofia: Sofia here - engineering manager, I care about latency and ops.
[00:22] Anita: Dr. Anita Patel - clinical data lead, will evaluate quality and regulatory constraints.
[00:27] Priya (Redwood SE): Thanks. Goal for today: align on success criteria, model shortlist, workload sizing, and next steps for benchmarks.
[00:35] Michael: Right. Quick context - we currently run a rules-based triage + a small BERT ensemble for classification; looking to move to generative QA for summarization and question-answering across patient notes. Privacy is huge - data can't leave EU region for this POC, and we need KMS integration.
[00:55] Jordan: Understood. On Redwood side we can run this on Redwood Dedicated in the region you pick, or Private if you need an on-prem agent. For the POC Dedicated is typical.
[01:05] Sofia: Cost will be a concern - we need rough committed cost for a 4-week POC.
[01:10] Priya: We'll come back to sizing. First, can we agree success criteria? Michael, what would you measure?
[01:17] Michael: Primary: QA F1 > 0.82 on our clinical QA set. Secondary: average latency for a 1k-token-ish exchange under 300ms tail, throughput around 8-12 qps. Also hallucination rate below our current baseline.
[01:32] Anita: Also de-identification - any PHI must be redacted or processed under our controls. Audit logs and versioning required.
[01:40] Jordan: Good. So success = quality + latency + compliance gates. Now, model shortlist - Priya, can you run through recommended open models?
[01:48] Priya: Sure. Given clinical domain and multilingual (English + Spanish) examples, we usually shortlist: 1) Mistral-instruct-like (lighter but strong instruction following), 2) Llama-2 derivatives (65B for quality, 13B for low-latency), 3) MosaicML MPT-30B (good for long context), 4) Falcon family (good open-instruction variants), and 5) smaller RedPajama or student models for edge cases. We can also test quantized variants (4-bit/8-bit) to reduce cost.
[02:20] Michael: Any preference on fine-tuning vs retrieval-augmented generation (RAG)? We have a vector DB of de-identified notes.
[02:26] Priya: For clinical, RAG + targeted fine-tuning on your gold QA set usually yields best ROI. Fine-tuning takes more time (weeks) and data, RAG can get you quick accuracy gains. For the POC we recommend RAG + prompt engineering, and a smaller fine-tune experiment if your labeled set is >5k examples.
[02:45] Sofia: Latency for RAG vs end-to-end model? Will embedding + retrieval add too much latency?
[02:50] Priya: Good question - the extra retrieval hop adds ~10-50ms if cached locally, but network calls to remote vector stores add more. On Redwood Dedicated we host embedding and retrieval close to the model to keep tail latencies low.
[03:05] Jordan: Also consider prefix/KV cache; for interactive sessions with repeated prefixes (clinical prompt templates) we get token savings and faster responses.
[03:12] Michael: Benchmarks - what will Redwood run? We want representative clinical prompts; typical request is 300-800 input tokens, want a 200-400 token answer.
[03:21] Priya: We'll run three benchmark suites: latency (p90/p95), throughput (max sustainable qps with SLO), and quality (F1, exact match on held-out QA). We'll run with 8-bit/4-bit quantized models and FP16 baselines to compare. We'll also measure cost per 1k tokens.
[03:37] Anita: Please include tests for Spanish prompts, because a chunk of our notes are Spanish.
[03:43] Priya: Will do - multilingual tests included.
[03:45] Sofia: For workload sizing - what inputs do you need from us?
[03:48] Jordan: Token distribution and concurrency targets. Also expected daily volume.
[03:52] Michael: Current daily traffic for the QA flow is ~50k requests, peak concurrency 25-30, average payload ~700 tokens in, 300 out. For the POC sample we'll provide 500 annotated QA examples and a 10k-item de-id vector store snapshot.
[04:11] Priya: Excellent. Based on that, for a pilot at 10 qps sustained we'd recommend a small Dedicated cluster: 2x A100-like GPUs for 13B models or 4x for 65B depending on batching. For quantized 4-bit runs you can reduce to 1-2 GPUs for 13B. We'll give a concrete sizing doc.
[04:30] Michael: Can you also run a canary on our staging VPC?
[04:33] Jordan: Yes, we can route to your VPC for Private-style deployment - but that adds setup time. For speed we usually run Dedicated in the same region first.
[04:40] Sofia: Timeline wise - we want benchmarks and a short report within two weeks of sharing data. Feasible?
[04:46] Priya: Yes - if you share samples by Friday (2026-06-26) we can provision the Dedicated cluster and start runs, results by 2026-07-01. That matches what Jordan noted.
[04:56] Michael: Security: SOC2 and KMS - Redwood supports customer-managed keys?
[04:59] Priya: Yes, KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated. We'll share the integration guide. Audit logs are available in Redwood Console.
[05:08] Anita: Will the model see raw PHI? We need to ensure it's encrypted at rest, and access-controlled.
[05:12] Jordan: Data at rest encrypted, RBAC, and per-request audit logging. We'll include a security appendix.
[05:18] Michael: Ok model tradeoffs - can you summarize recommended pairings for POC?
[05:22] Priya: Shortlist pairings: (a) Mistral-instruct-like 7-15B quantized for fast latencies and decent instruction following, (b) Llama-2-65B FP16 for highest quality / hallucination reduction, (c) MPT-30B for long-context summarization tests, (d) Falcon-large or fine-tuned smaller variants for Spanish-heavy prompts. We'll run each with RAG and prompt templates.
[05:45] Michael: Costs - rough delta between 13B quantized vs 65B FP16 for POC?
[05:50] Priya: Rough rule: 65B FP16 is ~3-4x the GPU-hours and infra cost compared to a quantized 13B. We'll provide per-hour and per-1k-token estimates in the pricing doc.
[05:58] Sofia: Any pre-built eval harness? We want reproducible tests.
[06:02] Priya: Redwood provides an eval harness integrated into Redwood Console. We'll push the benchmark scripts and the results dashboard to you.
[06:10] Jordan: Next steps recap - Priya to provision cluster and run benchmarks on sample; Jordan to send pricing and Dedicated sizing; Michael to share sample dataset and success criteria; Sofia to confirm stakeholders. Schedule: kickoff next week.
[06:24] Michael: Quick note - we may be evaluating Anthropic for safety features; curious if Redwood has safety tooling or guardrails we can enable.
[06:30] Priya: Redwood has safety hooks, content filters, and the ability to chain an external safety model. We'll include safety config examples.
[06:37] Anita: Please flag any changes needed for handling PHI in RAG pipelines - we need the chain-of-custody documented.
[06:44] Priya: We'll add that to the security appendix.
[06:47] Jordan: Anything else?
[06:48] Sofia: No, that covers it.
[06:50] Michael: Thanks everyone. We'll send the sample and a meeting invite for the benchmark kickoff.
[06:55] Jordan: Great, we'll follow up with docs and pricing. Bye.

--- End transcript ---
